Setting up w11 (0.4.0) ...

w11: wdotool, wwmctl, wxprop, wxrandr, warandr and wmirror are on PATH.

  * On GNOME, the window commands need the bridge extension, and gnome-shell
    only scans extension directories at login: LOG OUT AND BACK IN ONCE.  The
    extension is installed and is enabled for you automatically in that first
    session.  wxrandr and warandr work already; until the relogin the window
    commands say the bridge is not running and name gnome/install-bridge.sh,
    which is the from-a-clone route -- this package has done that part.
  * /dev/uinput is now open to the user at the active seat (udev rule
    60-w11-uinput.rules), which is what lets wdotool type and click
    without root.  Anyone who can open it can type as you -- see the threat
    model in /usr/share/doc/w11/README.md.gz.
  * On an X11 session the tools hand over to the real ones; install those
    with: apt install xdotool wmctrl

Processing triggers for libc-bin (2.43-2ubuntu2.3) ...

Running kernel seems to be up-to-date.

No services need to be restarted.

No containers need to be restarted.

No user sessions are running outdated binaries.

No VM guests are running outdated hypervisor (qemu) binaries on this host.

Setting up w11 (0.4.0) ...

w11: wdotool, wwmctl, wxprop, wxrandr, warandr and wmirror are on PATH.

  * On GNOME, the window commands need the bridge extension, and gnome-shell
    only scans extension directories at login: LOG OUT AND BACK IN ONCE.  The
    extension is installed and is enabled for you automatically in that first
    session.  wxrandr and warandr work already; until the relogin the window
    commands say the bridge is not running and name gnome/install-bridge.sh,
    which is the from-a-clone route -- this package has done that part.
  * /dev/uinput is now open to the user at the active seat (udev rule
    60-w11-uinput.rules), which is what lets wdotool type and click
    without root.  Anyone who can open it can type as you -- see the threat
    model in /usr/share/doc/w11/README.md.gz.
  * On an X11 session the tools hand over to the real ones; install those
    with: apt install xdotool wmctrl
